reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds one shared isNonWorkingDay predicate that every weekend site now calls, rather than re-implementing the check per site.

duplication.why: Adds no new copied block, but threads holidays through four pre-existing copies of the 'skipWeekend ? (daily ? skip : move) : date' decision (getNextDate, schedule-template, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange) instead of consolidating them, so each copy had to be edited in parallel.

placement.why: The non-working-day rule and the date-moving loop live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend helper; the type change sits in the model type and the serialisation in rule-utils.

scope.why: Focused on holidays; widening getDatesInRange's look-around window from 2 to an unexplained 14 days is related but a magic number.

maintainability.why: The predicate is clean, but getDateWithSkippedWeekend's unknown-mode branch is contorted, the 14-day window is unexplained, and future weekend-rule changes still require touching four sites that each pass holidays by hand.

one_place.where: What counts as a non-working day lives in isNonWorkingDay and the moving rule in getDateWithSkippedWeekend (shared/schedules.ts); getNextDate, schedule-template, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange all call them, though each still decides locally when to apply them and passes holidays itself.
